findings.title: Reserve repeated identifier text comparisons before coordinate expansion
findings.cause: The per-criterion product reservation depends on selector element counts, not identifier lengths. Public criterion_applies rebuilds selector sets and compares the positive client selector on every coordinate before a later platform mismatch. No candidate is produced, so output text reservations never account for these repeated comparisons. Initial input-byte reservation is one-time and does not grow with this product.
findings.qualification: Isolated actual _Generation.expand with real immutable record/criterion/requirements and public criterion_applies. Call-local context/client seams supply already-assessed values; no whole-snapshot or suite execution. CountedIdentifier delegates str equality/hash unchanged. Equal-character counts are the summed lengths of compared equal strings, not elapsed time or a claim about CPU instructions. Input text hashing may be cached; the observed repeated positive equality still compares equal distinct strings. The positive client match is followed by a platform mismatch, so no output copy or serialized-output reservation can cover this repeated text work.
findings.required_change: Reserve a conservative aggregate text-comparison/hash/traversal bound before the product, or eliminate repeated work with a prospectively bounded selection stage that preserves public applicability semantics. Include a deterministic long-identifier negative with zero candidates, a sufficient-capacity positive control, and rejection before counted comparisons when capacity is short. Do not use elapsed-time assertions.
